extracted.intended_audience: public water systems and State drinking water regulators responsible for implementing the Lead and Copper Rule (40 CFR part 141)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and operational standards for public water systems to control corrosion, manage source water treatment, maintain service line inventories, validate inventory accuracy, and implement service line replacement plans under the Lead and Copper Rule (40 CFR part 141).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum orthophosphate or silicate residual when inhibitor used
rubrics_metrics.description: If a corrosion inhibitor is used, maintain a minimum orthophosphate (as PO4) or silicate concentration measured in all tap samples that the State determines is necessary to form a passivating film on pipe interior walls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When orthophosphate is used: for OCCT designations for systems previously without corrosion control treatment, orthophosphate must be >= 0.5 mg/L (as PO4); for systems previously with corrosion control treatment, >= 1.0 mg/L (as PO4), unless the State determines the minimum is not technologically feasible or not necessary for OCCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alkalinity minimums or ranges if adjusted
rubrics_metrics.description: If alkalinity is adjusted as part of OCCT, the system must maintain a minimum concentration or a range of alkalinity measured at each entry point to the distribution system and in all tap samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values and measurement locations must be those the State determines reflect OCCT or re-optimized OCCT (see paragraph (f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: State determination of OCCT water quality parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Values for water quality parameters (e.g., pH, alkalinity, orthophosphate, silicate) used to reflect OCCT or re-optimized OCCT must be those the State determines appropriate for the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State may designate additional parameters it determines reflect OCCT. The State must notify the system in writing of these determinations and explain the basis for its decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous operation and monitoring of OCCT
rubrics_metrics.description: All systems (including consecutive systems and systems not required to monitor under §141.87) must continue to operate and maintain OCCT and maintain water quality parameters at or above State-designated minimums or within designated ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all water quality parameter samples collected under §141.87(b)(4) through (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-month compliance determination and excursion threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with OCCT maintenance is determined every six months; a system is out of compliance for a six-month period if it has excursions for any State-specified parameter on more than nine days cumulatively during the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An excursion occurs when the daily value for one or more water quality parameters at a sampling location is below the minimum or outside the State-designated range. States may exclude obvious sampling errors from the calculation but must record them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily value aggregation rules for water quality parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for calculating the 'daily value' for a water quality parameter at a sampling location: average multiple measurements collected the same day; use the single measurement if only one; use the most recent prior daily value if no measurement collected that day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If EPA approved an alternative aggregation formula under §142.16(d)(1)(ii) in the State program revision, the State's formula must be used in lieu of the formula in paragraph (g)(2). Continuous monitoring and grab samples are aggregated the same way.

rubrics_metrics.name: State modification of OCCT determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: A State may modify its OCCT determination or optimal water quality parameters on its own initiative or in response to a written request by a water system or other interested party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be in writing with supporting documentation. The State may require a CCT study to support modification. Revised designations must be in writing, set forth new treatment/parameter requirements, explain the basis, and provide an implementation schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA review and Federal determination authority on OCCT
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA Regional Administrator may review State OCCT determinations and issue Federal corrosion control treatment determinations where the State failed to act by deadlines, abused its discretion, or where the technical aspects would be indefensible in Federal enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to procedures in §142.19; applies to determinations under paragraphs (d), (f), or (h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate assessment when tap lead > 0.010 mg/L — Step 1 sampling timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: When an individual tap sample under §141.86 exceeds 0.010 mg/L and the site is included in the site sample plan, the water system must, within five days of receiving the result, sample a water quality parameter site on the same size main, same pressure zone, and within a half-mile radius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems without corrosion control treatment are not required to collect these samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameters to measure in Step 1 assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Step 1 corrosion control treatment assessment, the system must measure pH, alkalinity, orthophosphate (as PO4) when an orthophosphate inhibitor is used, and silica when a silicate inhibitor is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurements collected per paragraph (j)(1)(i) must be taken at the sampling location(s) identified in paragraph (j)(1)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 sampling location rules and adding sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems with an existing water quality parameter site that meets requirements can use it; systems required to meet OWQP but lacking such a site must add new sites until they have twice the minimum number listed in §141.87(b)(1)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When exceeding twice the number of sites, the State may determine whether newer sites better assess treatment effectiveness and may remove existing sites during sanitary survey evaluation of OCCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 site follow-up sampling timeframe and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of receiving tap sampling results >0.010 mg/L, the system must collect and analyze a follow-up lead sample at the tap site. Follow-up samples may use different volumes or collection procedures to assess sources of elevated lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-up samples must be submitted to the State but cannot be included in the 90th percentile compliance calculation under §141.86. If unable to collect, the system must provide documentation to the State per §141.90(g)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 evaluation and submission of treatment recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must evaluate Step 1 and 2 results to determine if localized or centralized OCCT adjustments or other distribution actions are necessary and submit recommendations to the State within six months after the end of the tap sampling period in which exceedance(s) occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrosion control modification may not be necessary for every exceedance; other actions include flushing. Systems optimizing or re-optimizing OCCT under paragraphs (a)–(f) need not submit a treatment recommendation. Recommendations should note cause of elevated lead if known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 4 State approval of treatment recommendation timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: The State must approve the water system's treatment recommendation or specify a different approach within six months of completing Step 3 and notify the system in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State must explain basis for its decisions in writing per paragraph (j)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 5 timeline for OCCT modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the State-approved recommendation requires adjustment of OCCT, the water system must complete modifications to corrosion control treatment within 12 months of receiving the State notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems without corrosion control treatment required to install OCCT must follow the schedule in §141.81(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 6 follow-up sampling after OCCT modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems adjusting OCCT must complete follow-up sampling within 12 months after completing modifications and submit sampling results to the State in accordance with §§141.86 and 141.87.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-up sampling must comply with §§141.86(c)(2)(iii)(D) and 141.87(b)(3) as cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 7 State designation of optimal water quality parameters (OWQP)
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems adjusting OCCT, the State must review the system's modifications and designate OWQP in accordance with paragraph (f) within six months of receiving the sampling results described in Step 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation must be in writing and explain the basis for the determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 8 operate in compliance after designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems adjusting OCCT must operate in compliance with the State-designated OWQP and continue tap sampling in accordance with §§141.86(c)(2)(iii)(E) and 141.87(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued operation and monitoring must follow paragraph (g) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water treatment Step 1: monitoring and recommendation deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A system exceeding the lead or copper action level must complete lead and copper source water monitoring (§141.88(b)) and make a treatment recommendation to the State (§141.83(b)(1)) no later than 180 days after the end of the monitoring period during which the action level was exceeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the first step in the source water treatment timeline under §141.83(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water treatment Step 2: State determination deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The State must make a determination regarding source water treatment within six months after submission of monitoring results under Step 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State must notify the system in writing and set forth the basis for its decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water treatment Step 3: installation timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If the State requires installation of source water treatment, the system must install the designated treatment within 24 months after completion of Step 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required installations must be properly installed and operated as designated by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water treatment Step 4: follow-up monitoring timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The system must complete follow-up tap water monitoring and source water monitoring within 36 months after completion of Step 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-up monitoring is used by the State to review the installation and operation of treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water treatment Step 5: State specification of maximum permissible source water levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The State shall review samples taken before and after installation and determine maximum permissible lead and copper concentrations for finished water entering the distribution system within six months after completion of Step 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such levels should reflect the contaminant removal capability of the properly operated and maintained treatment designated by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water treatment Step 6: continued operation and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The system must operate in compliance with State-specified maximum permissible lead and copper concentrations for finished water and continue source water monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A system is out of compliance if the level at any sampling point is greater than the State-designated maximum permissible concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: System treatment recommendation content
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system exceeding the lead or copper action level shall recommend in writing the installation and operation of one of the source water treatments listed (ion exchange, reverse osmosis, lime softening, coagulation/filtration) or may recommend no treatment if it demonstrates treatment is not necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommendation is submitted to the State per §141.83(b)(1) and must be supported by monitoring data and any demonstration materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: State determination options for source water treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: After evaluating source water samples, the State shall determine whether source water treatment is necessary; if necessary, the State shall require installation of the recommended treatment or another treatment from the listed options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the State requests additional information, the water system must provide it by the date specified. The State must notify the system in writing and explain the basis for its decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper installation and operation of designated source water treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each system shall properly install and operate the source water treatment designated by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper operation is required to achieve the contaminant removal capability used to set maximum permissible source water levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: State review to set maximum permissible finished water concentrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The State shall review source water samples taken before and after treatment installation and designate maximum permissible lead and copper concentrations for finished water entering the distribution system, reflecting the removal capability of the treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State must notify the system in writing and explain the basis for its decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued operation and maintenance requirement for source water treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each water system shall maintain lead and copper levels below the maximum permissible concentrations designated by the State at each sampling point monitored under §141.88.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System is out of compliance if any sampling point exceeds the maximum permissible concentration designated by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification of State source water treatment decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may modify its determination regarding source water treatment or maximum permissible finished water concentrations on its own initiative or in response to a written request; requests must explain why modification is appropriate and provide supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A revised determination must be written, set forth new treatment requirements, explain the basis, and provide an implementation schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA authority for source water treatment decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA Regional Administrator may review State treatment determinations and issue Federal treatment determinations where the State failed to issue determinations by applicable deadlines, abused discretion in a substantial number of cases or affecting substantial populations, or where technical aspects would be indefensible in expected Federal enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to procedures in §142.19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service line inventory requirement (material and location)
rubrics_metrics.description: All water systems must develop a service line inventory that identifies the material and location of each service line connected to the public water distribution system, including both portions where ownership is shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory must include all service lines regardless of ownership status and meet the detailed requirements in §141.84(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial and baseline inventory submission deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: All water systems must develop an initial inventory and submit it to the State by October 16, 2024. All systems must develop a baseline inventory and submit it by the compliance date in §141.80(a)(3); newly regulated systems must develop a baseline within a State-established schedule not to exceed three years from when they become subject to the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline inventory must include each service line and identified connector regardless of ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connector material categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Connector materials must be categorized in the baseline inventory as: 'Lead' (connector made of lead), 'Non-Lead' (determined by evidence not to be lead), 'Unknown' (material not known), or 'No connector present' (no connector at location).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Water systems are not required to identify specific material of a non-lead connector but may use the material (e.g., copper) as an alternative to 'Non-Lead'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service line material categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Each service line or portion where ownership is shared must be categorized as 'Lead', 'Galvanized Requiring Replacement', 'Non-Lead', or 'Lead Status Unknown'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems may provide more information regarding unknown service lines so long as unknowns are clearly distinguished from categorized lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address or unique locational identifier requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventory must include a street address associated with each service line and connector; where street addresses are not available, a unique locational identifier (e.g., block, GPS coordinates, intersection, or landmark) may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies to every service line/connector entry in the inventory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility of inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventory must be publicly accessible. Water systems serving greater than 50,000 persons must make the inventory available online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly accessible inventory must include the information described in paragraphs (a)(2)–(4) and be kept updated as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement in lieu for systems with no lead/galvanized/unknown lines
rubrics_metrics.description: When a system has no lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead status unknown service lines, no known lead connectors, and no connectors of unknown material, it may comply by providing a written statement instead of a full publicly accessible inventory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must include a general description of all applicable sources used to make the determination (see paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) and (b)(2)). Instructions to access the inventory or statement must be included in the Consumer Confidence Report per §141.153(h)(8)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual inventory updates and submission to State
rubrics_metrics.description: All water systems must update the baseline inventory annually with new information and submit updates to the State in accordance with §141.90(e)(4). Updates begin one year after the compliance date in §141.80(a)(3). The publicly accessible inventory must reflect updates no later than the State submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some systems (only non-lead) are exempt from submitting updates unless they later discover lead lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of materials for lead-status-unknown by replacement deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: All water systems must identify the material of all lead status unknown service lines by the applicable mandatory service line replacement deadline in paragraph (d)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification is required as part of annual updates and validation activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when previously non-lead line discovered as lead
rubrics_metrics.description: If a water system discovers a service line previously inventoried as non-lead is actually lead or galvanized requiring replacement, the system must update the inventory, notify the State in accordance with §141.90(e), and comply with any additional State-required actions to address the inaccuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may trigger replacement and reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer notification and offer to inspect disputed categorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a consumer or customer notifies the water system of a suspected incorrect categorization of their service line material, the system must respond within 30 days with an offer to inspect the service line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response timeframe is required to ensure consumer concerns are addressed promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of non-lead service line category — validation pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems must validate accuracy of the non-lead service line category by identifying a validation pool consisting of all service lines categorized as 'non-lead' excluding records showing installation after June 19, 1988 (or applicable later dates), visual inspections already confirming non-lead, or previously replaced lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation pool rules are in paragraph (b)(5)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation confirmation method and sample size rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm service line material of a random sample of non-lead service lines from the validation pool by visual inspection of the pipe exterior at a minimum of two points. Where ownership is shared, inspect each portion. Systems must validate at least as many lines as required by Table 1 to paragraph (b)(5)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Random selection methods (e.g., random number generator) are required; inspection must include at least two external visual points. Table 1 specifies percent or counts by size of validation pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 validation sample sizes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These numbers specify minimum validations required per paragraph (b)(5)(ii) Table 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate when physical access is not granted for validation
rubrics_metrics.description: If physical access to private property is necessary but the water system cannot gain access, the system is not required to validate that site and must replace it by randomly selecting a new service line from the validation pool to conduct validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must document inability to access and follow random replacement rules per paragraph (b)(5)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines for inventory validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines for completing inventory validation: (A) No later than December 31 following seven years after the compliance date in §141.80(a)(3) for certain systems; (B) a State-established deadline for systems on a shortened replacement schedule; or (C) a State-established deadline no later than three years prior to mandatory replacement deadline for systems using deferred or extended schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific applicability of each deadline is described in paragraph (b)(5)(iv). Systems must follow the applicable deadline established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and reporting of validation results
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that conduct validation must complete validation by the applicable deadline, submit results in accordance with §141.90(e)(9), and submit the specific inventory version (including date) used to determine the number of non-lead lines in the validation pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must comply with State instructions and any additional corrective actions for inventory inaccuracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of inventory validation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems may request a waiver of the inventory validation requirements by submitting documentation to the State demonstrating the system conducted an inventory validation at least as stringent as required and obtaining written State approval of the waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The waiver request must be in writing and supported by equivalent validation documentation as set out in paragraph (b)(5)(vi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service line replacement plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All water systems with one or more lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead status unknown service lines must create and submit a service line replacement plan by the compliance date and ensure the plan is sufficiently detailed to enable compliance with inventory and replacement requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must be submitted to the State in accordance with §141.90(e) and be updated annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement plan: strategy to determine unknown service line materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must describe a strategy for determining the material composition of lead-status-unknown service lines in the inventory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategies could include targeted inspections, records review, or other approved methods as described under paragraph (c)(1)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement plan: standard operating procedure for full service line replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must include a standard operating procedure (SOP) for conducting full service line replacement (e.g., replacement techniques).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOP should ensure consistent and appropriate replacement methods to minimize disturbance and exposure (paragraph (c)(1)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement plan: communication strategy before replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must include a communication strategy to inform consumers and customers before a full or partial lead or galvanized requiring replacement service line replacement, consistent with notification and mitigation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication must meet the notification and mitigation requirements in paragraph (h) of this section and §141.85(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement plan: flushing and particulate lead mitigation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must include a procedure for consumers and customers to flush service lines and premise plumbing of particulate lead following disturbance of a lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead-status-unknown service line and following full or partial replacement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure must be consistent with requirements for notification and mitigation in paragraph (h) and §141.85(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement plan: prioritization strategy including environmental justice considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must include a strategy to prioritize service line replacement based on factors including known lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines and community-specific factors, such as populations disproportionately impacted by lead and populations most sensitive to lead effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritization should consider community risk and equity factors (paragraph (c)(1)(v)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement plan: funding strategy and customer assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must include a funding strategy for conducting replacement and, where the system intends to charge customers for replacement costs, describe whether and how the system intends to assist customers unable to pay for the portion they own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding description should explain customer charge approach, any assistance programs, and legal basis under State/local law or tariff agreements (paragraph (c)(1)(vi)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement plan: communication strategy to inform customers and consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must include a communication strategy to inform residential and non-residential customers and consumers (property owners, renters, tenants) about the service line replacement plan and program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan should specify how and when communications will be made and tailored to distinct customer groups (paragraph (c)(1)(vii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement plan: identification of laws/regulations affecting access and cost-sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must identify any laws, regulations, and/or water tariff agreements that affect the system's ability to gain access to conduct full replacement and any provisions that require customer consent or authorize/require customer cost-sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify citations to specific provisions that affect access or payment arrangements (paragraph (c)(1)(viii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement plan: strategy for lead-lined galvanized service lines
rubrics_metrics.description: If the system identifies lead-lined galvanized service lines in the inventory, the plan must include a strategy to determine the extent of their use and categorize any lead-lined galvanized lines as lead pursuant to table 2 to paragraph (d)(6)(iii)(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System should document methods for identifying and classifying lead-lined galvanized lines (paragraph (c)(1)(ix)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement plan: deferred deadline documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems planning to use a deferred deadline: the plan must include documentation showing eligibility (10% of known lead and galvanized requiring replacement service lines in the replacement pool exceeds 39 annual replacements per 1,000 service connections), identification of deferred deadline and associated cumulative average replacement rate and schedule, and information supporting infeasibility of earlier replacement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific calculations, annual numbers, duration, and feasibility justification are required as described in paragraph (c)(1)(x)(A)-(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access and online requirement for replacement plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The service line replacement plan must be accessible to the public; systems serving greater than 50,000 persons must make the plan available online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan accessibility supports transparency and public participation (paragraph (c)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual update requirement for replacement plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems must annually update the service line replacement plan to include any new or updated information and submit updates to the State on an annual basis per §141.90(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual updates ensure the plan reflects current inventory, replacement progress, funding, and prioritization changes (paragraph (c)(3)).
